item.title: Lughole 0.4.0
item.description: - **Change a channel's instrument.** Click the guitar button on any channel. Lughole listens for the notes being played and plays them again on any of 128 built-in instruments (pianos, guitars, strings, brass, synths and more) or your Riff Pad sound. For drums, choose Follow the rhythm and every hit plays a note or chord you pick. Add the result as a new channel or replace the original.

item.title: Lughole 0.3.1
item.description: - **Add an empty channel.** Click the + New channel row at the bottom of a document, or choose Audio > Channels > Add Empty Channel (⌃⌘N), to add a silent channel alongside the others.

item.title: Lughole 0.3.0
item.description:
- **Channel headers.** Every channel now has a header beside it. Click the name to work on just that channel (⌘-click to pick several), drag it up or down to reorder, and use the icons to mute, duplicate or delete it. A channel's name and settings now stay with it when it moves.
- **Samples in the Riff Pad.** Select part of any recording and choose Use Selection as Riff Pad Sample (⌥⌘K). It joins the Riff Pad's sound list and plays across the keyboard from its original pitch.
- The version number is shown in the status bar.

item.title: Lughole 0.2.0
item.description:
- **Separate instruments.** The new Stems tab splits a song into vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano and everything else, right on your Mac. Open them as channels you can mute, solo and balance, as separate files, or keep only the parts you want (untick Vocals for a karaoke version).
- **Riff Pad.** A keyboard synth in its own window (⌘K). Play or click in a short riff, then drag it onto a channel to mix it in, or onto the new "+ New channel" row to add it as a channel of its own.
- Fixed a crash when saving a newly generated document, and one when adding a channel.

item.title: Lughole 0.1.0
item.description: - First release: a native audio editor for macOS. Open almost any audio (and the sound from video), fix voices with one click, edit channels, generate tones, and save to WAV, AIFF, CAF, FLAC, AAC, Apple Lossless, MP3, Opus or Ogg.
